clue.text: Pedestrian is for it, I see

parts.note: pro means in favour of
it, in old slang, is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: the phrase 'I see' is taken for its spoken sound, two letter names said aloud

parts.note: the two words spoken are the letter names I and C

explanation.surface: Someone arguing that walking is something they support, and that they understand it.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO + SA + IC gives PROSAIC. 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic and pedestrian both describe something dull, ordinary and lacking imagination; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Pick fruit

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an instruction to harvest fruit, but 'Pick' is a noun meaning the best of the bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum role or plum job is the most desirable one, the choice selection; plum is also a common orchard stone fruit.

clue.text: Duty in paper round to turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Sun is a British newspaper
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A paperboy or papergirl's obligation is to show up for the delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: SUN + O, reversed upward, gives ONUS. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a responsibility or obligation that rests on someone, the same as a duty.

clue.text: Day on the water in craft, to reach peak in Scotland

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside, so the first part goes within the second

parts.note: art and craft are skill

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits beneath it, so the later word follows the earlier

parts.note: short for Thursday
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: A day spent boating before climbing a Scottish mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue means the water comes after the day. Arthur's Seat is the hill overlooking Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's Seat is the main summit of an extinct volcano in Holyrood Park, Edinburgh, so a Scottish peak.

clue.text: Short lift certainly in slight bend

parts.note: curt means brief, abrupt

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: yes is an affirmation, 'certainly!'

explanation.surface: A short ride in a car, certainly, with a little bend in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: CURT + YES reversed (SEY) gives CURTSEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a small bob made by bending the knees as a mark of respect, a slight bend of the body.

clue.text: Poking prostate, perhaps, the Church had a look

indicators.note: something poking into another pushes inside it, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: the prostate is an example of a gland, signalled by 'perhaps'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rather indelicate medical examination, with the Church investigating.
explanation.walkthrough: CE pokes into GLAND: GLAN(CE)D.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to take a quick look, so glanced in the past tense matches had a look.

clue.text: Food not right, throws away rubbish

indicators.note: 'not right' asks for the abbreviation of the word right to be taken out of the word before

parts.note: grub is informal for food
R is the abbreviation for right
to bin something is to discard it

explanation.surface: Someone discards food that has gone off as garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUB without R is GUB, then BINS. Gubbins is British slang for odds and ends or junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is informal British slang for miscellaneous junk, worthless stuff or clutter, much like rubbish.

clue.text: Prayer kept up by the Vatican

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom upward
the letters are kept inside the following words, held within them

parts.note: letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A prayer preserved by the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: thE VAtican holds EVA, which read upward gives AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave, short for Ave Maria (Hail Mary), is a Catholic devotional prayer to the Virgin.

clue.text: Stuffing mushroom too much, a gargantuan starter, that is, for dish

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside something, so the following material is packed within it

parts.note: the cep is a prized edible mushroom, the porcini
OTT is over the top
taken as written

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: its first letter
i.e. is Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: An overstuffed mushroom as a gigantic appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT + A + G stuffs CEP: C(OTTAG)EP, then IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage pie is a British dish of minced beef topped with mashed potato and baked in the oven.

clue.text: Cut, little girl fixed bandages

indicators.note: a bandage wraps around a wound, so one part is wrapped around the other

parts.note: to dish is to ruin or rig, so fixed as in a fixed contest
a mini is a small one, here a little miss

explanation.surface: A little girl has been patched up with bandages after a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the wound but is the definition, an adjective meaning reduced. 'Dish' as a verb means to ruin or rig, as in a fixed match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut has been reduced in size or amount, which is what diminished means as a past participle.

clue.text: A turbulent, catastrophic life ultimately too much to explain

indicators.note: a catastrophic event leaves things in ruins and wildly disarranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word before

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A life so turbulent and disastrous that it defies description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the material; 'catastrophic' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Unutterable describes something too great or extreme to be expressed in words, beyond saying.

clue.text: Corporation tax unwarranted methinks, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that corporation tax is unjustified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old word for a potbelly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is dated humorous slang for a large paunch, and tum is a familiar word for stomach or belly.

clue.text: Breakfast — inspiration in general, might you say?

indicators.note: asking how you might say it points to the spoken form rather than the spelling

parts.note: a muse is a source of inspiration; Lee was the Confederate general Robert E. Lee

explanation.surface: Wondering whether breakfast is a source of inspiration in general.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSE followed by LEE, spoken together, sounds like the cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit, typically eaten as a morning meal; definition by example.

clue.text: Fall onto bed finally, as weary

indicators.note: one thing dropped onto another lands on top of it, so the second part follows on from the first
finally points to the closing letter of the word before

parts.note: its last letter
rain falls, and a fall of rain is a shower

explanation.surface: Collapsing into bed at last because you are so tired.
explanation.walkthrough: RAIN is placed onto D, giving D + RAIN. 'weary' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain someone is to exhaust or tire them out, which is a transitive sense of weary.

clue.text: Put out about an agent causing disorder, spy screened

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part goes around the other

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out
taken as written
a germ is a microbe that causes disease

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a troublemaking agent, with a spy kept hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: DOUSE goes about AN + GERM: D(ANGERM)OUSE. 'Put out' looks like angry, but it is extinguish. 'screened' means shown on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger Mouse is the secret-agent hero of a British animated television series, so a spy seen on screen.

clue.text: Animal with others, those commonly happy hamsters, say?

parts.note: 'them' for 'those' is common, non-standard usage
feeling up means in good spirits
hamsters are an example of pets

explanation.surface: An animal among others, perhaps a cheerful family of pet hamsters.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal is the wild drummer among Jim Henson's puppets, so the capital is a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal is a member of the puppet troupe, so Animal together with Kermit and company makes up the whole cast.

clue.text: Possibly an electrified train, not having run off the rails, getting in earlier

indicators.note: earlier says this part is placed at the front of the rest
a train off the rails is in disorder, so the letters are scrambled
not having something means it is left out of what follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written for rearranging
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A derailed electric train, with one carriage arriving early.
explanation.walkthrough: ELECTRIFIED TRAIN loses one R, is scrambled, and IN goes before it. 'Possibly' marks 'an' as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'an', like 'a', is the indefinite article in English grammar, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Saint punching angel, the recommended policy?

indicators.note: punching drives one thing into another, so it ends up inside

parts.note: angel and honey are both terms of endearment
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint hitting an angel, and asking whether that is the advised course.
explanation.walkthrough: ST goes into HONEY: HONE(ST)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says honesty is the best policy, so it is the course of action people advise; the question mark flags the allusion.

clue.text: Good to get out more then, after a touch of solitude

indicators.note: after puts the earlier part of the clue behind the later one
just a touch means only a small bit, the opening letter

parts.note: its first letter
if you get out more, you are at home less often

explanation.surface: Advice to someone isolated: be good and go out more after some time alone.
explanation.walkthrough: S + IN LESS. Getting out more means being in less, a playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinless means free from sin, morally pure, so it describes a good person.

clue.text: Support outstanding female actress

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an inflatable life jacket that keeps a person afloat
second meaning: the American film star known for her curvy figure

explanation.walkthrough: Second World War airmen named their life jacket after the buxom actress; 'outstanding' plays on her bosom as well as her fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mae West was an RAF life vest that held wearers up in water, and Mae West was a celebrated Hollywood star.

clue.text: Astride horse, judge set off

indicators.note: sitting astride means straddling, legs either side, so one part sits around the other

parts.note: a trier is one who tries a case
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A judge sits on horseback and sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIER straddles GG: TRI(GG)ER. Trigger was also Roy Rogers's horse, an extra layer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, start it or cause it to happen, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Fish's bitter partner

parts.note: bitter is a style of British beer
a wife is a spouse

explanation.surface: A fish's resentful spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, bitter is a hoppy pale beer, so it gives ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American herring-family fish of the Atlantic coast, an example of a fish.

clue.text: See 14
Matter at home filling sink

indicators.note: filling something places material inside it

parts.note: to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A household problem with the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: IN fills POT: PO(IN)T. 'sink' looks like a noun but is the snooker verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Point and matter both mean the issue under discussion, as in 'the point at hand' or 'the matter at hand'.

clue.text: Keeping rhythm, eventually

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in step with the beat
second meaning: after a while, sooner or later

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a musician who finally finds the beat; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing in time means matching the beat; things that happen in time come about after a period, later on.

clue.text: Lazy Arsenal about to pick up old footballer

indicators.note: about means around, so one part surrounds the other
a lazy arrangement is slack and sloppy, so the letters are loosely reordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: An idle Arsenal side poised to sign a veteran footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; jumbled to ALANSER, it goes around HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Shearer is a retired English striker, the Premier League's record goalscorer, so a former footballer.

clue.text: Every other character into meatballs — and the rest

indicators.note: every other character means alternate letters are taken, skipping one each time

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Every other person diving into the meatballs, and everyone else too.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al. is the Latin abbreviation for et alii, meaning 'and others', used in lists and citations.

clue.text: Priest the typical rabbi backs

indicators.note: the backs of words are their final letters

parts.note: last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A priest supporting a typical rabbi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like support or a reversal, but here it means the ends of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the high priest in the Old Testament Book of Samuel who raised the boy Samuel.

clue.text: Ugly cut hampering big cat, almost desperate for perfect cure

indicators.note: hampering something gets in its way, here sitting in the middle of the other part

parts.note: the mullet is a notoriously unflattering haircut

indicators.note: desperate behaviour is frantic and wild, so the letters are thrown about
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A desperate search for a cure for a big cat with an ugly wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ugly cut' looks like an injury but is a hairstyle, short at the front and long at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic bullet is a remedy or solution that cures a problem completely and simply, with no side effects.

clue.text: Taken from the bottom, butt stain

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom means going upward, backwards

parts.note: to butt with the head is to ram

explanation.surface: A cigarette end picked up from the floor, leaving a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or blemish, and to stain is to discolour or sully; both verbs mean damage the look of.

clue.text: See 22
Enduring bird in duck, dropping head

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
dropping the head loses the first letter

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A long-suffering bird among the ducks, ducking its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The head is dropped from the duck before the bird goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, without end; enduring means lasting a long time, so they are close synonyms.
